sources.entry: FluxMarkdown - Quick Look extension for Markdown previews with Mermaid, KaTeX, GFM, TOC, and charts. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/xykong/flux-markdown) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: FluxMarkdown is a macOS Quick Look extension that renders Markdown files with Mermaid diagrams, KaTeX math, GFM, a TOC panel, and Vega/Graphviz charts when you press Space in Finder.
summary.what_it_does: It adds Quick Look previews for many Markdown file extensions (.md, .mdx, .qmd, .rmd and others) in macOS Finder, using bundled local assets for rendering. It supports Mermaid diagrams, KaTeX math, GFM tables, task lists, strikethrough and GitHub Alerts, plus syntax highlighting for 40+ languages. Charts are supported through Vega, Vega-Lite and Graphviz (DOT). The app also offers an interactive table of contents, YAML frontmatter rendering, zoom and pan, scroll-position memory, and light, dark or system themes. Export to PDF (Cmd+Shift+P) and HTML (Cmd+Shift+E) is available, and read-only .tsv table previews are included.
use_cases: preview Markdown files in Finder without opening an editor
view Mermaid diagrams and flowcharts from README or notes files
render KaTeX math in Markdown documents
export Markdown notes to PDF or HTML
preview Vega or Graphviz charts embedded in Markdown
how_to_run: Manual: download FluxMarkdown.dmg from Releases, open it, and drag FluxMarkdown.app to Applications
Build from source: git clone <repo URL>, cd flux-markdown, make install
If Gatekeeper blocks the app: xattr -cr "/Applications/FluxMarkdown.app"
If QuickLook does not update: qlmanage -r
notable: Quick Look preview inside Finder with Space, no separate editor needed
Dual-licensed: GPL-3.0 for open source, commercial license for closed-source use
Bounded read-only TSV previews with row, column and cell limits
Install via Homebrew cask or DMG
caveats: Sends pseudonymous usage statistics and checks for updates by default; can be turned off in Settings
Commercial use in closed-source products requires a paid commercial license
TSV previews are read-only, capped at 500 KiB, 1,000 rows, 100 columns and 20,000 cells, and do not support quoted multiline fields or non-UTF-8 encodings
Very large TSV files can use significant memory on initial open
summary.license: GPL-3.0 (open source); commercial license available from the author
